Store & Connectors Expansion

Where we left off (Aug 14): the structured-location grill for itsbrex/allman-cli#1 was built but never answered — the grill → spec → tickets → implement pipeline stalled at its first gate — while the "next move" list (adopt the 21-issue upstream TUI backlog, triage, app.tsx split, README fix) and the connector-flavored upstream cluster (company records + CompanyEnricher boundary, multi-channel enrichment, A2A) were surveyed but untouched. This plan closes the loop: it locks in the four Round-1 location recommendations, makes the three Round-2 calls (query surface, migration, provenance), sequences fork-backlog adoption, proposes one thing we hadn't considered — a single Enricher connector contract, standardized while only one enricher exists — and confirms run-from-source dev shims in both repos as the auto-refresh mechanism, per Bun's own docs. All execution lands on feat/store-connectors-expansion in both repos.

What the history says

Mined from the Aug-14 sessions in both project histories. Three threads were live when work stopped. Store: itsbrex/allman-cli#1 (structured geo on connections) got a full research pass — geoUrn and countryCode are already fetched from the LinkedIn graph and discarded at profile-detail.ts:259 — and an interactive grill page (allman-cli plan #001, still untracked) whose four questions were never answered; Round 2 (query surface, migration, staleness) was declared but never run. Feature expansion: the 21 upstream TUI enhancements were surveyed with a decided process — audit which already shipped (#12 reactions, #6 snippets), adopt the rest as fork issues with the Upstream: join key, then triage — and the fork tracker still has zero issues. Connectors: upstream #10's comment thread proposes a provider-neutral CompanyEnricher contract (per-field provenance, never-overwrite-asserted) that the session judged "an open design negotiation" — unfit as a first ticket, but exactly the shape our geo provenance stamp is converging on independently.

Division of labor stays CLI-first: the CLI owns the store, the domain vocabulary, and every guarded write; the TUI reads the store from disk and shells out through spawnAllman. Every feature below splits into a CLI data-model half and a TUI surface half, in that order.

Dev workflow: what Bun's docs actually recommend

Asked-for "hot-build of linked binaries" resolves like this: Bun documents --watch (hard process restart on change), --hot (soft reload for long-lived Bun.serve processes), and bun build --watch (bundle rebuild) — and documents no combination of --compile with --watch. The dev-link system already installed in both repos sidesteps the whole question: ~/.local/bin/allman and allman-tui are symlinks to shims that exec bun src/index.*, so every invocation runs the current working tree with zero build step, and the TUI shim exports ALLMAN_BIN at the sibling CLI shim so the dev TUI always drives the dev CLI. Both links verified live today. A watch-recompile daemon would re-solve this at higher cost; the only thing it buys is dist/ parity, which bun run build covers on demand before a release.
